correctness.rationale: On the finite summand the defect is D=B*B−I and the logarithmic-concavity difference is B*WB with B invertible. The two diagonal conditions and det W=(a²−1)(b²−a²)−a²|u|² give the exact stated region, and det D is nonnegative there. Multiplying the proposed basis by q gives q, az and z²,z³,…, which is a bounded invertible finite-coordinate change from the monomial basis; division by q is bounded and invertible because |u|<ab. The model intertwines directly. The cleared two-by-two matrices of R and H are positive on this region, including the degenerate boundaries; their determinant conditions check directly from the stated gamma, eta and x. Thus R is positive with diagonal less than 1, 1−tR is nonvanishing, and the defect decomposition is a sum of positive Schur products. The space has independent evaluations and the kernel is normalized and nowhere zero, so the normalized Pick criterion applies. At (2,3,1), det W=11, det D=23, and the 22 entry of D−A*DA is −18, so failure of ordinary concavity persists on an open subset of strict logarithmic concavity. verify.py was inspected, not run; its real rational examples are consistency checks, not evidence for all complex u.
